newsitem.title: ITALY: Strike paralyses train travel in Italy.
newsitem.headline: Strike paralyses train travel in Italy.

text.p: A 24-hour rail strike paralysed Italy's train network on Sunday.

The strike, which began on Saturday night and ends at 2000 GMT on Sunday, was called by the rail unions to demonstrate their opposition to a plan by Prime Minister Romano Prodi to reorganise the state-run Ferrovie dello Stato railway system.
Prodi's directive, issued last week, would split the railway company in two by the end of 1997 -- one managing the rail lines and infrastructure and the second the train and rolling stock.
Unions are unhappy with the bulk of the plan and a move to abolish free rail tickets for staff and their families.
The government has scheduled talks with the unions on Tuesday in hopes of avoiding more industrial action planned for later this month.
The rail unions have called another 24-hour strike for next weekend and more protest for February 23.
State airline Alitialia said in a statement that it was adding domestic flights on Sunday to accommodate travellers seeking to reach their destinations by air.
